Empirical Research Plan
———————————————————————

1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (with an event-study extension and several robustness variants, i.e., triple-Diff and firm-fixed-effects IV).  
Logic: Aggregate shocks that tighten the supply of bank credit (e.g., 1998 crisis, 2001 recession, 2007–2009 crisis, and quarters in which the Fed’s Senior Loan Officer Survey (SLOS) reports net tightening) are plausibly exogenous to any individual non-financial firm. Firms differ ex-ante in how much they rely on banks versus public debt markets. Comparing outcomes of bank-dependent (“treated”) firms to otherwise similar market-access (“control”) firms before vs. after a credit-supply shock identifies the causal effect of a contraction in loan supply, holding constant aggregate demand conditions that both sets of firms face.  

Formally:  
y_it = α_i + γ_t + β (BankDep_i × Tight_t) + X_it′θ + ε_it  

where y_it is (i) probability of issuing a loan vs. a bond, (ii) total debt raised, (iii) investment (CapEx), or (iv) sales growth. β is the credit-supply effect.

Event-study coefficients δ_k obtained by interacting BankDep_i with dummies for each event-time k validate the parallel-trend assumption and show dynamics.

2. Treatment and Control  
• Treatment variable: BankDep_i – a time-invariant dummy equal to 1 if, over 1990–1994 (pre-period), >75 % of the firm’s external debt came from syndicated loans or the firm is unrated by S&P/Moody’s. Sensitivity checks use (i) a continuous share of bank debt, (ii) size-based quartiles.  
• Control group: Firms with public debt ratings whose bank-loan share <25 % in 1990–1994 (i.e., have reliable bond-market access).  
• Treatment timing: Tight_t = 1 in quarters classified as severe loan-supply contractions. Baseline Tight_t equals 1 if SLOS net-tightening > +20 pp OR aggregate bank NPL ratio is in the top quintile. Alternative definitions use (i) crisis dummies: 1998Q3–1999Q2, 2001Q1–2002Q2, 2007Q3–2009Q2; (ii) quarters with bank-stock index return < –15 %.  
• No running variable → not an RDD.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of a loan-supply shock, outcomes of bank-dependent and control firms would evolve similarly. Plausibility: Both groups are large publicly listed firms spanning the same industries and business cycles. We will test for pre-trend equality in the event study.  
A2. Shocks reflect supply, not demand: SLOS tightening and bank NPL spikes are driven by bank balance-sheet health, not by firm-specific demand. Since both treated and control firms face the same aggregate product-market demand, differential effects trace credit supply.  
A3. No differential anticipation: Firms cannot fully foresee and pre-empt shocks; the SLOS index is not released until after quarter-end.  
A4. Stable composition: Firms do not systematically switch from treated to control status in response to impending shocks because BankDep_i is fixed using the pre-period.  
A5. No spillovers strong enough to erase differences: Bond-market firms can tap public debt without binding quantity caps, so their outcomes are not mechanically constrained by spillovers from bank-dependent firms.

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  
T1. Differential product-market demand shocks (e.g., small firms in cyclically sensitive industries).  
Mitigation: Add firm*industry (4-digit NAICS) linear trends; include industry-quarter fixed effects; conduct placebo using sales growth as outcome in pre-period.  
T2. Endogenous selection into “dependence.”  
Mitigation: Define BankDep_i using a five-year window that ends well before the first shock; re-estimate on a matched sample (propensity-score match on size, Tobin’s Q, industry, rating).  
T3. 2008 bond-market stress (control group may also face quantity rationing).  
Mitigation: (i) Omitting 2008Q4–2009Q1; (ii) interacting BondStress_t (e.g., Baa-Aaa spread) with MarketAccess_i to net out bond-market frictions; (iii) triple-diff: BankDep_i × Tight_t × (1 – BondStress_t).

5. R Code Outline
```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)     # fast data handling
library(fixest)         # high-dimensional fixed effects
library(lubridate)      # dates

# 1. Load data
dat  <- fread("firm_quarter_panel.csv")         # merged Compustat-DealScan-etc.
tight <- fread("tightening_quarterly.csv")      # SLOS, NPL, bank stock returns
dat   <- merge(dat, tight, by = "fiscal_qtr")

# 2. Construct variables
# a. Bank dependence (pre-1995 average)
pre <- dat[fiscal_qtr < "1995-01-01",
           .(bank_share = mean(bank_debt / total_debt, na.rm=TRUE)), by = gvkey]
dep_cut <- 0.75
dat <- merge(dat, pre, by = "gvkey")
dat[, BankDep := (bank_share > dep_cut)]

# b. Tightening dummy (top quintile of SLOS net tightening)
q80 <- quantile(dat$slos_net_tightening, .80, na.rm=TRUE)
dat[, Tight := (slos_net_tightening >= q80)]

# c. Outcomes
dat[, InvRate := capx / lag(ppent, 1)]          # investment rate
dat[, LoanIssued := (loan_amount > 0)]
dat[, BondIssued := (bond_amount > 0)]

# 3. Baseline DiD: probability of issuing a loan
did_formula <- LoanIssued ~ BankDep*Tight + size + tang + leverage +
               fe(gvkey) + fe(fiscal_qtr)

est1 <- feglm(did_formula, data = dat, family = "logit")
summary(est1)

# 4. Event-study (-8 to +8 quarters around shocks)
forb <- as.formula(paste(
  "InvRate ~", 
  paste(sprintf("i(rel_time, BankDep, ref = -1)[%d]", -8:8), collapse="+"),
  "+ fe(gvkey) + fe(fiscal_qtr)"
))
est2 <- feols(forb, data = dat[abs(rel_time)<=8])
iplot(est2)

# 5. Robustness: drop 2008Q4–2009Q1
est_rb <- feglm(did_formula, data = dat[!(fiscal_qtr %between% c("2008-10-01","2009-03-31"))],
                family="logit")
etable(list(Main=est1, NoCrisisCore=est_rb))
```

6. Expected Results  
Theory (pecking-order with segmented credit markets) predicts β < 0: when supply tightens, bank-dependent firms (i) borrow less from banks, (ii) cannot fully substitute into bonds, leading to lower total debt and investment. Magnitude: during a severe shock, CapEx of treated firms may fall 5–8 percentage points of PPE relative to controls (≈25–30 % relative decline).

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)

C1: Parallel pre-trends shown? — 1  
C2: No anticipation / no simultaneous shocks? — 0.5  
C3: Stable treatment definition / no switching? — 1  
C4: No spillovers between groups? — 0.5  
C5: Common macro shocks absorbed by time FE? — 1  

Total ≈ 4/5.
